title: Set up your wallet
description: Create a wallet and write down your recovery words. If you stop partway through, you can finish the backup when you return.
journey: Create a wallet while it connects to the network.
Leave the backup unfinished, reopen the app, and finish it. Check that viewing the recovery words requires unlocking.
limitations: Save a backup file too. Winnow needs it to find your past payments when you restore the wallet.

title: Receive bitcoin
description: Label who an address is for, or what the payment is for, before sharing it. You can skip. Matching payments carry the local note in your wallet.
journey: Save a receive address label, request a new address and skip its label. Reopen the app and confirm that a payment to the old address still carries its note.
Confirm a payment on the test network and check that it appears in the wallet.
Watch a new payment arrive on Receive before it is confirmed, then check that its status updates after confirmation.
limitations: An address label does not verify the sender or create a payment destination. Labels stay on this device and are not included in wallet backups.

title: Send bitcoin
description: Choose an account, recipient, and amount. Check the address, fee, and total before sending or continuing to the account’s approvals.
journey: Enter an address and amount on the simple send screen.
Edit a reviewed payment, then verify the new amount, full address, fee, and total before sending.
Check that Bitcoin Core received the payment, open its details, and wait for the app to show it as confirmed.

title: Pay someone again
description: Name someone you’ve paid, or save their payment card. Next time, choose them in Send.
journey: Send to a new address, open that payment in Wallet, save the recipient, and rename them.
Reopen the app and check the name on the payment. Remove and re-add the saved recipient without losing the label.
Choose a saved address in Send and check the address-reuse notice. Pay a saved card, then check that the next payment uses a fresh address.

title: Name who paid you
description: Give a received payment a local name without attaching an address. Add a payment card or explicitly choose a destination before sending.
journey: Save a name-only label on a received payment, relaunch and check that the label persists.
Verify that a name-only person cannot send until a destination is attached.
Explicitly select a locally reconstructed funding address and continue through the normal amount and confirmation flow.
limitations: Funding addresses are unverified destinations, not proof of who paid you. Winnow never selects one automatically. Sending to an address again can reveal address reuse.

title: Choose a funding destination
description: If you choose to consult an explorer, review what is disclosed and whether the request goes directly or through Tor. Then explicitly select any returned destination.
journey: Open the funding-address lookup and review the transaction ID and network route before giving consent.
Choose a returned address explicitly, even if the explorer returns only one.
Save the destination with its unverified origin visible.
limitations: The explorer receives the transaction ID. Direct mode reveals your connection IP; a clearnet explorer reached through Tor sees an exit IP. Returned addresses do not identify people.

title: Save with other people
description: Choose who shares the wallet and how many approvals a payment needs. With two approvals out of three, one person can be away and the other two can still pay.
journey: Create shared savings from Wallet and choose who can approve payments.
Back up the funded account from its detail screen, then open Send, choose a saved recipient, and check the account, amount, and fee.
Continue straight to approvals without copying the request into another screen. Complete two approvals without the third person.
limitations: For shared control, each person must keep their own key. If you choose just one required approval, any one of them can spend.

title: Combine your phone with another signer
description: Use 2-of-2 MuSig2 so your phone and a separate key must both approve every payment. You can also use a MuSig2 group as one cosigner in a larger threshold vault.
journey: Set up an account with one key on the phone and another generated by Bitcoin Core.
Receive test funds and save a backup that includes the account.
Use Send to review the account, address, amount, and fee, then continue directly to the second-signer screen.
Leave a signing exchange, then start again with fresh signing data.
Review and approve on the phone, exchange replies with Core, and confirm a payment with one on-chain signature.
Restore the earlier backup with the recovery words and check that it finds the payment and the remaining balance.
In a separate flow, approve on the phone and share the raw request with a MuSig2 group acting as one signer. Import the group’s reply through Approve a request, then send.
limitations: Bitcoin Core 31.1 is the tested second signer. A hardware wallet needs its own compatibility test. Keep the wallet backup file, the phone’s recovery words, and a separate backup of the other signer’s key. Every key is required.

title: Back up and restore
description: Save a backup file with your payment history and shared accounts. Keep your recovery words too. You need both to restore the wallet and sign again.
journey: Export a backup with private keys and one without them.
Restore a wallet that has funds and check that the backup is valid and the funds are found.
limitations: Keep both your recovery words and your backup file. The words alone won’t restore your payment history.

title: More options when you need them
description: Start with the basics. Turn on Advanced mode in Settings to adjust fees and manage network connections.
journey: Check which tabs and controls appear in normal mode.
Turn Advanced mode on and off, checking that fee and network settings appear and disappear.

title: Inspect and import signing policies
description: Create a Taproot vault from public signer keys and coordinate approvals using PSBT text. Inspect the policy and reviewed transaction explicitly.
journey: Create a vault through the advanced form.
Import an approval request, review it, and contribute the device’s signature.

title: Replace a pending payment with a higher fee
description: Review a replacement’s fee and change before authorizing it. The original remains visible as replaced.
journey: Disconnect the test node before sending. Reopen the app, find the pending payment, then reconnect and check that the same payment reaches the node.
Use Bump fee, review and sign the replacement, then confirm it and inspect the app’s history.

title: Inspect peers and control external disclosure
description: Inspect connected peers and network settings. Explorer links open only after an explicit warning about the information sent to that website.
journey: Open the real peer settings.
Open an explorer warning and cancel before leaving the app.
Reset and shuffle the remembered peers, and watch fresh connections arrive.
limitations: Explorer websites are not wallet backends. A single or coordinated set of peers can still withhold information; multiple connections are not proof of independent operators.

title: Refresh the peer list
description: Download dated candidates from Winnow’s census without interrupting active peers. Reset and shuffle peers is a separate action.
journey: Choose Refresh peer list in Advanced settings, then read the observation date and candidate counts.
Keep your active connections while the new list becomes available for future connections.
If a refresh fails, keep using the previous valid list. Reset and shuffle remains a separate choice.
limitations: Downloads expire after seven days, then automatic selection falls back to bundled candidates. Bundled and downloaded census entries count as the same trust source. Every selected peer still undergoes normal wallet checks.

title: Use Tor for wallet connections
description: Turn on Tor to route peers, discovery, census refresh and explorer lookups through the embedded client. Networking stops in the background.
journey: Turn on Tor in Advanced settings and wait for Ready.
Return to the app after it has been in the background and let Tor reconnect.
If Tor fails, retry or explicitly turn it off. Winnow never silently switches to a direct connection.
limitations: Tor failure leaves Winnow offline. External browsers use their own routing; Winnow warns before opening them. I2P transport is deferred.
